# The only skips a CI run is allowed to have.
#
# One substring per line, matched against the reason unittest printed. A skip
# whose reason matches nothing here fails the job — see .github/ci/run_suite.sh
# for why that is a failure rather than a note.
#
# The list is short on purpose. The CI jobs install Godot 4.7.2, Blender 5.2.2
# and ffmpeg, which between them clear every conditional skip the three suites
# have except the ones below. If you find yourself adding a line, the question
# to answer first is whether CI could simply satisfy the dependency instead.

# tools/release/tests reads a real exported Windows build, and building one
# needs Godot's Windows export templates and a `butler` login — a release step,
# not a per-push one (docs/RELEASING.md). Six tests. The code paths they cover
# are also exercised against synthetic .pck fixtures by the tests either side of
# them, so what is lost in CI is the end-to-end assertion, not the coverage.
no build yet

# Note what is deliberately NOT listed: the purchased packs. assets_licensed/ is
# gitignored and no runner will ever have it, so the obvious expectation is a
# row of skips for it — and there is not one. The converters' tests run on
# fixtures they build themselves, the licence guard's tests build throwaway
# repositories, and the game draws self-authored stand-ins when the packs are
# absent, so all three suites run their full count against a checkout that has
# only assets_licensed/.gdignore in it. If a licensed-asset skip ever starts
# appearing, that is a test that quietly stopped covering anything on a clean
# clone, and this file is right to fail the job over it.
